main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling food (sambal belacan) in the shared kitchen; the group ends up with D cooking it on weekends only.

A-B.evidence: B agreed with A's no-strong-smell request (turn 2). A accepted cooking after 7 (turn 11), while B said smell is still a problem after 7 (turn 8) and proposed weekends (turn 17). A never commented on the weekend plan, so the alignment is only partial.

A-C.evidence: C complained about the smell on laundry (turn 3), supporting A's cause. C's objection (turn 9) conflicts with A's after-7 plan, but C accepts weekends (turn 20). A said nothing about it.

A-D.evidence: D initially refused to stop cooking (turn 4). A moved to the after-7 compromise (turn 11). D offered to cook at other times (turn 6) and accepted weekends (turn 18). A never explicitly endorsed weekends.

B-C.evidence: Both objected to the smell (turns 2, 3) and the after-7 plan (turns 8, 9). Both rejected the door and laundry fixes (turns 13, 14). B proposed weekends and C accepted (turn 20).

B-D.evidence: D resisted at first (turn 4). B proposed weekends (turn 17), D accepted (turn 18), and B thanked D (turn 19).

C-D.evidence: C complained about the laundry smell (turn 3). D agreed to cook on weekends (turn 18), and C said 'Weekends are fine for me too. Thanks, Agent D' (turn 20).
